of Pn−1 in n points in general linear position. We show that this inclusion is asymptotically an equality.
For this we use that XΣ is a toric variety and the asymptotic behaviour of complete linear series on them
can be managed through convex geometry. As a consequence, the vertical slices of ∆x(L) are NObodies
associated to a ray of divisors on XΣ with respect to a generic (strict transform) linear ﬂag. Lastly, the
global (gluing all t ⩾0) NObody on this special ray of divisors on XΣ is exactly the convex set described
in the statement, as we are able to prove the existence of sections whose valuation are the vertices of the
simplex.
For box-products of arbitrary degrees the vertical slices of ∆x(L) are still a family of NObodies on XΣ
with respect to general linear ﬂags. But it is harder to guess the vertices. It seems an interesting problem
to ﬁnd an algorithm that starts with a polytope in Rn−1 that is a NObody on a toric variety with respect to
a T-invariant ﬂag, and construct another polytope, that will be a NObody on the same toric space but with
respect to a generic linear ﬂag.
In dimension n ⩽3, we can ﬁnd non-trivial sections on XΣ, whose valuations provide the vertices of a
slice of the global NObody on XΣ with respect to general linear ﬂags. More precisely:
Theorem 1.2. Let X = C1 ×...×Cn be a product of smooth complex projective curves, polarized by a box
product L = L1 ⊠...⊠Ln with degLi = di. Assume d1 ⩾d2 ⩾... ⩾dn > 0. Let x ∈X be any point.
• If n = 2, then ∆x(L) is the isosceles trapezoid with vertices (0,0), (d2,d2), (d1 +d2,0), (d1,d2).
• If n = 3, then ∆x(L) is the convex hull of the 9 points (0,0,0), (d3,d3,0), (d2,d3,d2−d3), (d1,d3,d2−d3),
(d1 +d2 −d3,d3,0), (d2 +d3,0,d2 +d3), (d1 +d3,0,d2 +d3), (d1 +d2,0,2d3), and (d1 +d2 +d3,0,0),
In both cases, the shapes degenerate to the simplex in Theorem 1.1 when di = 1 for all i, while when the
di are not all equal the shapes are not simplicial.
It turns out that the verticies of our iNObodies from Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 happen exactly when
there is a change in the associated base loci of the graded linear series Wt
•. These ideas are generalized by
the authors in [FL25b] on any projetcive variety X by connecting three aspects of local positivity of a line
bundle L on X at a point x ∈X. On one hand we have inﬁnitesimal successive minima, then jets and ﬁnally
polytopal upper and lower bounds on the generic iNObodies. Moreover, in [FL25c] the authors study the
shape of generic iNObodies on Jacobians in small dimensions. The main issue here is realizing at least
asymptotically the family Wt
• as complete graded linear series on a modiﬁcation of Pn−1. For example, for
non-hyperelliptic Jacobian threefolds, Wt
• becomes complete on a birational model of P2 that is far from
being toric, while for the hyperelliptic case we may need to go to the Zariski–Riemann space.
The paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we review the Newton–Okounkov body construction
and their basic properties. In Section 3 we use intersection theory, positivity, toric geometry and Euclidean
volume computations to understand the vertical slices as Newton–Okounkov bodies on XΣ. In Section 4
we treat the case of dimension n ⩽3. In Section 5 we use particular incomplete linear systems on XΣ to
prove that the vertices of the simplex from Theorem 1.1 do belong to the iNObody, concluding its proof.
In Section 6 we state and motivate some open questions.
